assumptions.original: The progressive real integrand belongs to the probability-time L² domain. The driver is scalar Brownian relative to a filtration satisfying the usual conditions, with finite sample measure and a positive construction horizon T. The deterministic times satisfy s≤t≤T; the interval may be empty.
assumptions.reconstructed: eta is strongly progressive for F and (omega,r)↦eta(r,omega) is in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). B satisfies standard scalar Brownian finite-dimensional distributions: for every finite nonnegative time set S, (B_s)_{s∈S} has centered Gaussian law with covariance (s,t)↦min(s,t), and B has continuous paths mu-a.e. In particular B_0=0 is required almost surely, not for every sample, is strongly adapted to F, and B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for every s≤t. F is right-continuous and every subset S⊆Omega with mu(S)=0 belongs to F_t for every t≥0. s≤t and t≤T.
assumptions.evidence: Full-module binder and definition audit: hInc identifies the actual increment a.e. with the terminal integral of restrictAt t minus restrictAt s; hRep is the exact indicator of Ico s t; terminal isometry then gives the displayed product integral.

conclusion.original: The increment of the actual completed Itô process between two deterministic times is in L². Its squared expectation equals the probability-time energy of the original integrand on that cell. Formula: \mathbb E[(I_t-I_s)^2]=\int_{\Omega\times[s,t)}|\eta(\omega,u)|^2\,d(\mu\otimes du|_{[0,T]}).
conclusion.reconstructed: I is the specified continuous completed Ito integral of eta against B: the canonical elementary-integral limit off its null uniform-Cauchy exceptional set, zero on that set, and constant after T. Let D(omega)=I(t,omega)-I(s,omega). Then D∈L²(mu) and ∫D²dmu=∫_{Omega×[s,t)}eta(v,omega)²d(mu⊗lambda_T)(omega,v).
